answer.generated: Centroids and medoids serve as representative points in nearest neighbour smoothing to approximate the underlying distribution of data. A centroid is typically computed as the arithmetic mean of all points, minimizing squared Euclidean distance to all others, whereas a medoid finds the most centrally located data point, which is more robust to outliers. Both approaches help smooth decision boundaries by generalizing local patterns, but medoids are less sensitive to extreme values, making them preferable when noise is present.
